items.title: Library supplement: Finite Gaussian Hermite feature sums

source.anchor: F3 in source-only.json; proof topology literal finite-sum definition.
source.attribution: Original generic exposition of Gaussian polynomial and finite Hermite features; existing proofs reused without a novelty or primary-textbook completion claim.

items.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma_E=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\) be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. Let \(H_j\) be the unnormalized probabilists Hermite polynomial and put \(h_j(w)=[x\mapsto H_j(\langle w,x\rangle)]\in L^2(\gamma_E)\). For a finite set \(S\subset\mathbb N\) and real coefficients \(c_j\), put \(F_{S,c}(w)=\sum_{j\in S}c_jh_j(w)\). This declaration defines the indicated finite sum in the actual Hilbert space. It imposes no unit-vector, parity, positivity or normalization condition.
assumptions: The finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures are the actual structures on the same carrier \(E\).
\(\gamma_E\) is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. No positive dimension restriction is imposed.
\(S\) is any finite set of natural degrees, including the empty set. The coefficients are arbitrary real numbers.

bindings.boundary: These are finite polynomial and actual Gaussian Hilbert-space results. Infinite-series limits and application-specific force identities require separate proofs.

assumption_deltas.source: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure; gamma_E is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. H_j is the unnormalized probabilists Hermite polynomial, with Gaussian squared norm j!. L2 means the actual real square-integrable equivalence-class Hilbert space.
assumption_deltas.lean: Concrete finite-dimensional real inner-product normed and Borel structures on E, stdGaussian E and Lp real 2.

assumption_deltas.source: For every finite set S of natural degrees, real coefficient function c, and ambient vector w, define the finite L2 sum F_(S,c)(w)=sum_(j in S)c(j) h_j(w), where h_j is the preceding actual Hermite class. Empty S, degree zero and arbitrary signed or zero coefficients are allowed.
